subject: Where Logic keeps the English text of a label, and why a corpus of .strings could not find it
question: Of the tables whose translations this repository can cite, how many ship English at all, and can the English be addressed by the same key?

reverify.cost: ~25s; reads the app bundle, launches nothing

method: Walked every `.nib` in the bundle and separated them by how Apple localizes them. For the base-internationalised ones, read the archive's class table and paired each `NSLocalizableString` with the `NSString` that follows it, which is where Interface Builder puts the `.strings` key. Joined the result against each translated locale's overlay by key, and checked whether any of those tables also ships an `en.lproj` overlay. Then asked what each nib population would close if it were added to the corpus, before adding any of it. The two citations below are read back through `Scripts/logic_canon.py resolve`: key 300557.title in KeyCommands and key 3.title in AAFExportView.

canon.used_for: the string #895 opens with: citable in Korean at this same key and, before this change, provably absent in English

conclusion: Logic keeps the English text of 162 label tables inside `Base.lproj/<table>.nib` and ships no `en.lproj/<table>.strings` for a single one of them, so a corpus built from `.strings` had no English for any of those tables and answered ABSENT for every English label in them. The English is addressable: Interface Builder stores the `.strings` key next to the text, and joined by that key 6188 of the overlay's 6216 keys agree while NOT ONE key is nib-only -- so English can be cited at the same address as its own translations rather than in a namespace of its own. The 28 keys left over are numeric placeholders and two literal DO-NOT-LOCALIZE tokens. The second-order effect is larger than the first: with English and its translations in one namespace, 1828 more English values are known to be TRANSLATED by Apple, and 'Apple does not translate this' is the answer that exempts a literal comparison from needing a LabelSet -- so before this, the permissive answer was being given for 6270 labels on no evidence. `NSLocalizableString` is a base-internationalization construct and the other 1007 nibs have none, so this reader yields nothing from them; measured before deciding, their 3374 English values close none of this repository's uncitable literals, and sweeping them in on a cell-title filter would also sweep in Interface Builder's own defaults.
limits: Base.lproj only. 407 nibs sit in no `.lproj` -- 312 of them MAPlugInGUI plug-in screens -- and 600 more are fully localized per locale in the old style. Their labels are plain `NSString` under cell titles, mixed with Interface Builder's defaults (`Item 1`, `Header Text`, `$LN`), so reading them needs a filter nothing has measured. Named in SOURCES.json as a gap, and filed as #902.
Presence is not use. A label compiled into a nib may belong to a screen the running code never shows, exactly as for `strings`.
The three tables with no overlay in any locale name a `.strings` file that is not on disk. That is the address the overlay WOULD use; the English is real and the screen is untranslated.
`translated.en.u32` is a 32-bit digest set, so it can call an untranslated string translated -- the direction that asks an author for a LabelSet they may not need. It cannot do the reverse.
